answer: New identities start hollow, with zero history and near-zero weight, so swarming the network with fresh keys costs real stake while gaining almost nothing. Each agent stakes a decaying bond that shrinks by a fixed delta every epoch; at dawn, peers attest only to agents whose bond survived. An attacker must fund every sock-puppet at full bond and keep paying the decay to stay credible, making mass identity creation economically irrational compared to honest participation. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
